topic.name: Finding the Common Ratio of a Geometric Sequence Given Two Terms

question.text: Find the common ratio of the geometric sequence whose fourth term is $8$ and whose seventh term is $216.$
question.explanation:
To find the common ratio $r$ of a geometric sequence given two terms $a_m$ and $a_n,$ we use the formula

\[ r^{n-m} = \dfrac{a_n}{a_m}. \]

In this case, we're given $a_7 = 216$ and $a_4 = 8.$ Substituting $n=7$ and $m=4$ into the formula, we have

\begin{align*} r^{7-4} &=\dfrac{a_7}{a_4}\\[5pt] r^3 &= \dfrac{216}{8}\\[5pt] r^{3} &= 27. \end{align*}

Finally, by solving the equation for $r,$ we get

\begin{align*} r^3 &= 27\\[5pt] r^3 &= 3^3\\[5pt] r &= 3. \end{align*}

question.text: Find the common ratio of the geometric sequence whose fifth term is $7$ and whose tenth term is $-224.$
question.explanation:
To find the common ratio $r$ of a geometric sequence given two terms $a_m$ and $a_n,$ we use the formula

\[ r^{n-m} = \dfrac{a_n}{a_m}. \]

In this case, we're given $a_{10} = -224$ and $a_5 = 7.$ Substituting $n=10$ and $m=5$ into the formula, we have

\begin{align*} r^{10-5} &=\dfrac{a_{10}}{a_5}\\[5pt] r^5 &= \dfrac{(-224)}{7}\\[5pt] r^{5} &= -32. \end{align*}

Finally, by solving the equation for $r,$ we get

\begin{align*} r^5 &= -32\\[5pt] r^5 &= (-2)^5\\[5pt] r &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-2}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Common Ratio Using a Formula Given Two Non-Consecutive Terms

question.text: Find the common ratio of the geometric sequence whose sixth term is $-15$ and whose ninth term is $-\dfrac{3}{25}.$
question.explanation:
To find the common ratio $r$ of a geometric sequence given two terms $a_m$ and $a_n,$ we use the formula

\[ r^{n-m} = \dfrac{a_n}{a_m}. \]

In this case, we're given $a_9 = -\dfrac{3}{25}$ and $a_6 = -15.$ Substituting $n=9$ and $m=6$ into the formula, we have

\begin{align*} r^{9-6} &=\dfrac{a_9}{a_6}\\[5pt] r^3 &= \dfrac{\left( -\dfrac{3}{25} \right)}{(-15)}\\[5pt] r^{3} &= \dfrac{1}{125}. \end{align*}

Finally, by solving the equation for $r,$ we get

\begin{align*} r^3 &= \dfrac{1}{125}\\[5pt] r^3 &= \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right)^3\\[5pt] r &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{5}}. \end{align*}
